To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tetrahedral P 4 and As 4 molecules can be stabilized by encapsulation in the cavities of a polymeric or spherical host matrix.

the tetrahedral P 4 and As4 molecules can be included as guest molecules into the voids of polymeric host structures, which are stabilized by the formation of four intermolecular contacts between the E4 molecules and the polymeric chains.

the inclusion of E4 tetrahedral guests into a polymeric matrix or into spherical macromolecules stabilizes the tetrahedral structure, thus allowing for the first time the X-ray structural determination of these compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the structural characterization of the unstable E4 molecules (E = P or As) and their encapsulation into polymeric or spherical molecular hosts, which are able to stabilize the tetrahedral molecules and prevent their polymerization.
the synthesis, structural characterization, and chemical reactivity and stability of molecular and polymeric compounds containing E4 tetrahedral guests.
the stabilization of the tetrahedral molecules P4 and As4 by their inclusion into polymeric and spherical host molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E4 molecules are fixed by the host compound, and that the host-guest interactions in 1 and in 2 are comparable to the interactions between E4 and the host compound in [Ag(h- As4)2]1 [pftb].
the tetrahedral Pn and Asn molecules are stabilized in the solid state by inclusion into the polymeric or spherical host molecules.
the tetrahedral P 4 and As 4 molecules are stabilized by their inclusion into the voids of a host compound, which is a polymeric chain of the [Cu 2Cl 2{Cp 1 Fe(h -P 5)} 2] 1 molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it was not only possible to stabilize the tetrahedral P 4 and As 4 molecules in the solid state, but also to obtain the first structural characterization of yellow arsenic in the form of the compound [Ag(h- As 4) 2 ][pftb], which is stable under air and light for several days.
we have succeeded in the synthesis of polymeric and spherical coordination compounds that are capable of including intact tetrahedral P 4 or As 4 molecules as guest species.
we were able to stabilize the unstable tetrahedral E4 (E P, As) in the solid state by inclusion in polymeric and in spherical host molecules, and to characterize them by X-ray diffraction methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a host molecule not only enhances the stability of the As4 molecules, but it also decreases their molecular motion in solid state.
the use of a suitable host molecule is a powerful method to stabilize and characterize unstable molecules.
the encapsulation of P4 and As4 molecules in host compounds is a promising method for the structural investigation and stabilization of these highly reactive and unstable tetrahedral elements.
